findings.explanation: The root README identifies the paper product, and the tracked tree includes its manuscript, statistics, analysis, saved image and three subordinate Git links. Root-relative input/output paths support the structural common-root finding; this does not establish payload availability.

The partial verdict has a specific recursive defect: root .gitmodules leads to raw_eyegaze, whose own .gitmodules names a host-local lab-eyetracking source. The recorded paper computation instead consumes released BIDS files. The assessment correctly limits the consequence and does not pretend to have tested remote access.

The Docker recipe explicitly installs the scientific distributions, while Docker-Makefile installs the independently pinned REMoDNaV package. That meets the instrument’s inclusion interpretation without requiring vendored copies of every Python distribution.

I verified Git tree identities for the root code, manuscript and configuration. Missing material in this text-only capture cannot demonstrate untracked original work; overriding a checkout-cleanliness interpretation is justified.

The manifest inventories annex symlink keys for large image layers, and the raw dataset explains annex-managed content. The saved image manifest plus annex attributes corroborate large-content versioning independently of whether the payload bytes were supplied for review.

Partial is supported by the inherited label computation: its native record identifies inputs and outputs but no exact environment. The paper’s 2023 run does link img and results_def.tex to container/image and its Git tree. A missing main.pdf run is only unverified build coverage, since no compiled main.pdf is delivered in the assessed tree.
findings.suggested_correction: Retain partial on the demonstrated label-environment gap; describe manuscript execution as unverified rather than implying a shipped PDF lacks provenance.

findings.explanation: The updated README supplies installation links, clone and execution commands. Its obsolete local-environment instructions are explicitly separated, so their mere coexistence is not the silent documentation/mechanism conflict prohibited by the instrument.

The results-containerized tag resolves locally to the cited 57d2565 run, whose command selects Docker-Makefile clean results_def.tex. The separate main.pdf command also has a matching Makefile target. This establishes a concrete starting point without establishing a newly successful replay.

The current paper source uses project-relative data and image paths. The recursively included labels component retains explicit user-specific initialdir values in both submit scripts, so partial is defensible for the stated component-inclusive scope. Those scripts are legacy, not evidence the current paper rerun uses that host.

Imports in the numerical source and its local REMoDNaV classifier/helpers map to declared scientific packages; pylab is provided by matplotlib and sklearn by python3-sklearn. The recorded inputs supply data before container execution, matching the explicit DataLad-import fallback. The recipe also supplies make, Inkscape, latexmk and TeX Live for the documented manuscript route.

The README names supported platforms and Docker-format constraints, but the invoked adapter assumes Docker is callable on PATH by the invoking user. The linked submit scripts additionally require a particular initial directory, Python executable and Condor environment. Partial accurately distinguishes documented primary prerequisites from residual assumptions.

The current route has an actual prerequisites list, installation pointers and a Debian-based package recipe. This narrower list-presence criterion can be met while must/011 remains partial for configuration assumptions; those are distinct properties.

The root Git tree contains both the build specification and container registration, and the image-build record names its Dockerfile input. This verifies version-controlled specification rather than assuming it from an environment filename alone.

History supplies executable build/save commands, a subsequent Dockerfile modification, and a later completed archive conversion. This is stronger than a one-time specification introduction: it demonstrates a maintained procedure and tracked update instances. The duplicate flag and matching should/008 verdict are correct.

The saved image is content-identified despite its descriptive latest tag: the adapter loads and runs the SHA256 image ID derived from the saved configuration. The 2023 run tree also names the same configuration hash in the original image layout. Floating recipe rebuild dependencies do not negate the archived execution environment’s identity.

The annex web log contains a public-looking content URL, but neither that log nor the captured source is a successful independent recipient retrieval. Under the explicit inspection-only boundary, not-checked is the appropriate result, rather than met or a claimed retrieval failure.

The updated instructions identify the host tools, DataLad clone, expected image transfer, named results replay and manuscript command; container registration supplies the matching archived-image invocation. Met is supported for this documented consumer route, without claiming the upstream labels README is current.

Root and subordinate components share Git commit identities; the two DataLad datasets add annex content identities within that same composition. A nonretrievable nested source URL concerns availability, not use of a common version-control mechanism.

The frozen history demonstrates a 2023 computation and later container maintenance, not an established regular paper-workflow test series. The linked Travis definition tests REMoDNaV separately and has no supplied completed-run receipts. Not-checked avoids turning absent CI evidence into an unjustified failure.

Separate raw and derivative input gitlinks, a software gitlink, root analysis code, an environment directory and figure-rendering targets provide concrete modular separation. The instrument does not require each internal directory to be a separate repository.

The 2023 native record reports exit 0 for the real numerical computation, not merely a proposed command. The configured adapter starts a new docker run container and removes it afterward. This supports historical fresh-container execution of the numerical pipeline; it does not prove the PDF build or a current replay succeeded.

The adapter’s docker run --rm and the registration’s temporary HOME establish disposable execution for the registered paper workflow. Bind-mounted project outputs remain persistent by design. Cleanup of HOME is conditional on success, but container disposal is still explicit.
findings.suggested_correction: Retain met. Replace the adapter’s version-tag-only citation with the frozen content-hash locator (or an independently established immutable commit URL); a release tag alone is not a strict immutable source locator.

findings.explanation: An initial image build, subsequent numerical use and a much later startup/format conversion do not establish regular reconstitution testing. The 2025 exit-0 command tests container startup, not scientific replay. The not-checked verdict correctly preserves that distinction.

The image is represented inside the dataset by its saved manifest/configuration and annexed layers, with successful save/conversion records. This meets archival inclusion as a structural property; missing review payloads and unverified current retrieval belong in the limitations and must/016.
The same executable maintenance history supports must/014 and should/008. The assessment explicitly marks the upstream duplicate instead of suggesting two independent update-process checks.

The raw-data documentation explicitly describes unrestricted access, while the software and paper have public licensing declarations. No access-controlled component is evidenced. Treating the local ancestral path as a linkage defect rather than proof of restriction correctly supports the empty-subject N/A.

There are genuine independently maintained code and data components, not merely package dependencies. Public Git links compose them, but the recursive raw dataset includes a machine-local source link. Partial is supported for the recursive component boundary and appropriately differs from N/A.

The root overview and module paths provide some structural guidance, but the inherited labels README still describes removed preprocessing/detection commands rather than the delivered compute_all.sh route. That is a concrete documentation gap supporting partial rather than an unexplained demand for more prose.

The cited evidence demonstrates revision-isolated gitlinks and an explicit relative raw-data interface. A legacy Condor initialdir and stale documentation demonstrate portability/documentation defects, but do not identify a dependency coupling or an independent update that breaks the current composition. The partial verdict therefore lacks criterion-specific support.
findings.suggested_correction: Identify a concrete cross-module interface or dependency constraint that prevents independent updates and justify partial from it. Otherwise reconsider met on the pinned boundaries, or use not-checked for update compatibility that was not established; do not use legacy host paths alone as evidence for this criterion.

findings.explanation: Gitlinks provide the composition mechanism, the container registration connects the saved image to the build file, and the native run connects selected inputs to results. The existence of this mechanism is supported even though particular nested links have separately identified defects.

The user-facing root README, discoverable module path/URL map and REMoDNaV’s package README provide navigation and usage tooling. The more specific recombination-documentation shortfall in may/002 does not negate the presence of these navigation aids.

limitations: Inspection only of the frozen manifest e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499 and its root-discoverable source/history graph. No network requests, payload acquisition, container builds or scientific workflow execution occurred.

Binary data, image layers, figure/style payloads and some historical blobs are omitted. An offline historical diff could not read a missing blob; the modified-path inventory and retained commit message were available. Git commands used GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1.

The manifest hash and 23 distinct cited source-file hashes were checked; six cited historical commits were located and their relevant records inspected. The root run tag was resolved locally. Source capture and historical exit codes do not independently certify present reproducibility or scientific validity.

The native checklist pin and assessment validator both passed. All 31 expected criterion IDs were present: MUST 12 met, 4 partial, 1 not-checked; SHOULD 6 met, 2 not-checked, 1 not-applicable; MAY 2 met, 3 partial. No aggregate score or explicit denominator claim is supplied in the assigned JSON. These are assessment status counts, not a review score.

The original probe receipt and companion report were not part of the assigned anonymized input and were not read. Probe overrides were checked against source evidence and native rules rather than accepted from the assessor’s description. No original complete working tree was available for a faithful full probe replay.

The external Docker adapter was inspected only through its root-README/configuration discovery path and the frozen file hash; no release-tag immutability or live deployment version was independently established.
This is an independent technical review, not human approval. No peer assessment or review was consulted.
